newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish opposition proposes more tele privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Danish opposition proposes more tele privatisation.

text.p: Denmark's opposition Conservative party on Thursday proposed a further 25 percent privatisation of telecommunications group Tele Danmark.
The telecoms group was partially privatised in 1994, leaving the state with a 51 percent stake.
The proposal was made as part of the Conservatives' negotiating package ahead of this autumn's all-party negotiations on Denmark's 1997 state budget.
The ruling Social Democrat-led centre-left minority coalition unveiled in late August its 1997 draft budget calling for deficit cuts and fiscal tightening.
Last year the Conservatives reached a pact with the government on the 1996 budget.
The idea of a further sellout of the government stake in Tele Danmark was part of a proposed 42.4 billion crown privatisation package mooted by the Conservatives.

The proposal, still very much subject to negotiation, calls for the possible divestment by the state of parts of Danish Rail, the government's remaining 51.3 percent stake in Copenhagen Airports, a data centre and the state football pools organisation.
